name: Deepfield
author: gurvinny
description:
Deepfield replaces Pelican Panel's default look with a cosmic-atmospheric UI, and ships two matching palettes rather than one: a deep-space dark theme and a cool observatory-white light theme, both built from a single set of colour tokens. The panel's own theme switcher picks between them - Deepfield only sets the default, so each user's choice stays theirs.

Behind every page a canvas starfield drifts in three parallax layers with mouse-driven motion and pooled meteors, over a slow-moving nebula fog you can hue-swap between violet, teal and rose. In light mode the metaphor inverts to a daylight sky with drifting motes and a soft aurora haze. Aurora gradients - cyan to teal to violet - mark primary buttons, active nav, focus rings and status badges, and never wash out, because the sidebar and modals stay heavily tinted and readable.

The in-server console gets its own treatment: a CRT monitor top bar, optional phosphor bloom and scanlines, and Start / Restart / Stop pills that glow in their own status colours. The xterm.js palette is patched at runtime to match the theme - four presets, including a 1:1 Minecraft vanilla palette for Paper, Forge and CurseForge servers.

Every effect is configurable from a native Filament settings page: starfield density, nebula hue, CRT bloom, scanline density, terminal palette, audio cues and reduce-motion. Values persist to .env, so they survive updates with no migrations. Typography is self-hosted - Orbitron display, Space Grotesk UI, JetBrains Mono code - with no CDN calls and no Google Fonts round-trip, and prefers-reduced-motion is always honoured.

Skins all three Filament panels: admin, app and server. Coexists with Theme Customizer - hand it the component colours with a single toggle. MIT licensed.
